solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Passage in chorale — it motivates recurring theme (9)

indicatorNotes.Passage in: a passage is a stretch of text, so a passage in the words is a run of letters taken from them

blocks.note: choraLE IT MOTIVates

annotation.surface: A music note: one stretch of a chorale carries the theme that drives the whole piece.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface is honest camouflage: a leitmotiv really is a musical idea, so the hidden answer sits right in its own scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a theme that recurs through a work, associated with a character or idea.

entries.clue: Jumbo pilot in middle row without uniform (5)

indicatorNotes.in middle: the letter in the middle of 'pilot' is the one taken
indicatorNotes.without: row is taken without the U for uniform

blocks.note: the middle letter of piLot
row = ARGUE; uniform = U in the NATO alphabet, and one U goes

annotation.surface: A jumbo jet's pilot sitting in the middle row, out of uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' and 'pilot' paint an airliner, but Jumbo is just the adjective for big. Row here is a quarrel, not a line of seats.
annotation.definitionFit: Jumbo means very large, as in a jumbo pack.

entries.clue: What’s infectious to do in zeal and in fun (9)

indicatorNotes.to do in: to do in is to wreck, so the letters that follow are smashed and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
anagram fodder, 5 letters

annotation.surface: A wry remark about how catching enthusiasm and fun can be.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests zeal and fun are what spreads; in fact the infectious thing is the flu, spelt out from their letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Influenza is a highly infectious viral disease, so it is what's infectious.

entries.clue: Married lad who waits up with Polish PA (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: M = married, as on forms
a page is a boy who attends or waits on someone; turned up it reads EGAP
to hone is to polish or sharpen

annotation.surface: A married waiter polishing up his Polish with a personal assistant's help.
annotation.walkthrough: PA reads as personal assistant beside a waiter, but it is a public address system, and 'Polish' only looks like the nationality because it opens the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a simple public address device for amplifying the voice.

entries.clue: Start of final death throe, done with struggle? (3,3,2,3,4)

annotation.definition: Start of final death throe, done with struggle?

indicatorNotes.Start of: the start of 'final' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.struggle: the letters struggle and twist into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of Final
anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram fodder, 4 letters

annotation.surface: The last spasm of a dying struggle, when the fight is over.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read plainly it describes a last gasp, which is exactly what the end of the road means.
annotation.definitionFit: The end of the road is the point where something, or someone, can go no further: finished.

entries.clue: Squash game avertible when one’s lacking fancy racket (9,6)

indicatorNotes.lacking: one's lacking: the I is taken out
indicatorNotes.fancy: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder once the I goes
one = I, removed from the fodder
a row is a racket, a loud noise

annotation.surface: A squash match that could have been avoided if someone hadn't lacked a smart racket.
annotation.walkthrough: Squash and racket set up the sport; both switch meaning. A vegetable marrow is a large British summer squash, like an overgrown courgette (zucchini).
annotation.definitionFit: The vegetable marrow is a variety of squash, Cucurbita pepo.

entries.clue: Spirits hostelry placed beside record player (5)

indicatorNotes.placed beside: the inn is set next to the DJ

blocks.note: a disc jockey plays records
an inn is a hostelry

annotation.surface: A pub serving spirits with a DJ spinning records beside the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: Spirits and hostelry make a drinking scene; the spirits are genies. 'Record player' is the person who plays records, not the machine.
annotation.definitionFit: Djinn (jinn) are spirits of Arabian and Islamic lore; the word is plural.

entries.clue: Launch cylindrical rockets (5)

indicatorNotes.rockets: rockets go up, and in a down entry up means bottom to top

blocks.note: tubed = made in the form of a tube, so cylindrical

annotation.surface: The launch of cylindrical rockets from a pad.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all space launch; 'rockets' is a verb telling the word to shoot upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance, the launch of a career or product.

entries.clue: Grand little room attached to surface of ice? (5)

annotation.definition: Grand little room attached to surface of ice?

indicatorNotes.surface of: the surface of a word is its first letter, the top in a down entry
indicatorNotes.attached to: G and LOO are joined on beneath the I

blocks.note: first letter of Ice
G = grand, a thousand
loo = the smallest room, a lavatory

annotation.surface: An odd little room that sits on top of the ice.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an igloo: a small room built on the ice. The loo, British for toilet, is traditionally called the little room.
annotation.definitionFit: An igloo is a small domed shelter built of snow blocks on the ice.

entries.clue: Impulsive conductor never promoting last quartet for cellos (5,4)

indicatorNotes.promoting last: the last letter is promoted, moved up the column
indicatorNotes.quartet for: a quartet is four, so four letters are kept for the entry

blocks.note: NEVER with its last letter R moved up two places
the first four letters of CELLOs

annotation.surface: A hot-headed conductor who never lets the cellos lead the final quartet.
annotation.walkthrough: The orchestra is a front: impulsive conductor means something that conducts impulses, not a rash maestro.
annotation.definitionFit: A nerve cell, or neuron, conducts electrical impulses.

entries.clue: Fleeing Man United in official three-quarter length anorak (7)

indicatorNotes.in: United is put in among the other letters
indicatorNotes.three-quarter length: only three of the four letters of GEEK are used

blocks.note: ref = referee, a match official
anorak = GEEK, a nerdy enthusiast; three of its four letters
U = united, as in club names

annotation.surface: A match official in a three-quarter-length anorak, with Manchester United in view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man United' is the football club, but the clue splits it: Fleeing Man is the definition. An anorak is British slang for an obsessive, nerdy enthusiast.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: someone who has fled war or persecution for safety abroad.

entries.clue: Hawker tethering large male bird (7)

indicatorNotes.tethering: the hawker ties up the L, holding it inside

blocks.note: to hawk is to clear the throat and spit, so a hawker is a gobber
L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A street hawker keeping a big cock bird tied up.
annotation.walkthrough: A hawker suggests a street seller or falconer; here it is someone who spits (gob is British slang for spit).
annotation.definitionFit: A gobbler is a male turkey, named for its call.

entries.clue: Nark delaying question about supply (5)

indicatorNotes.delaying: the Q is held back one place, coming after the U

blocks.note: to nark is to irritate, to pique
Q = question, the letter in PIQUE that is moved one place later

annotation.surface: A police informer stalling a question about where the goods came from.
annotation.walkthrough: A nark is also British slang for a police informer, which the surface leans on; here it is the verb to irritate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to kit someone out with what they need.

entries.clue: Bachelor leaving cast to be a month away (3,2,4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: a bachelor leaving is walking out, so B departs from the letters that follow
indicatorNotes.cast: cast as in cast metal: the letters are recast into a new shape

blocks.note: B = bachelor, removed
anagram fodder once the B goes

annotation.surface: A bachelor leaving the cast of a show for a month.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is theatrical: a performer leaving the cast. Cast is really the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrase-for-word synonym: someone out of the house is away, and 'not at home' is also the old polite line for refusing callers.

entries.clue: Fiddle duo could be flat (5)

blocks.note: to con is to fiddle, cheat
a second word for fiddle, making the duo: to do someone is to swindle them

annotation.surface: A pair of violins that might be playing out of tune.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is musical: two fiddles playing flat. In fact 'duo' asks for two words meaning fiddle, CON and DO, and flat is an apartment.
annotation.definitionFit: A condo, short for condominium, is an owned apartment, a flat.

entries.clue: Purging vomit has to choke gent cycling (9)

indicatorNotes.to choke: HAS chokes on the gent, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.cycling: the letters of SIR go round, last to front

blocks.note: to cat is British slang for to vomit
taken as written
gent = SIR, cycled so the R comes first

annotation.surface: A grim scene of a man choking on his own vomit as he is purged.
annotation.walkthrough: Purging and vomit fit together, which hides that vomit is just CAT, an old slang verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Catharsis is a purging, originally of the bowels, now usually of emotions.

entries.clue: All told about retired seaman with harpoon? (2,7)

indicatorNotes.retired: retired = withdrawn, gone back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: on = about, as in a book on birds
AB = able-bodied seaman; retired it reads BA
a harpoon is a kind of lance, a thrown spear; the ? marks the loose fit

annotation.surface: A yarn about an old sailor and his harpoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired seaman' reads as a pensioner, but retired is doing the reversing.
annotation.definitionFit: On balance and all told both mean taking everything into account.

entries.clue: Spur on person pressing cheese (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, on means placed above

blocks.note: a spur is an offshoot, like a branch or limb
one who presses or urges

annotation.surface: Someone being spurred on to press cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spur on' looks like one phrasal verb; split it and Spur is a noun, a branch, with on placing it above.
annotation.definitionFit: Limburger is a strong-smelling soft cheese from Limburg.

entries.clue: Young child tended to dash around pitch full of energy (9)

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so the word for dash is read backwards
indicatorNotes.full of: the pitch is filled with the E

blocks.note: to dash is to run; turned around it reads NUR
to pitch is to throw, to sling
E = energy, as in physics

annotation.surface: A small child told to race around a sports pitch, bursting with energy.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'tended': a nurseling is a child being nursed. Pitch looks like a playing field but is the verb to throw.
annotation.definitionFit: A nurseling is an infant being nursed or cared for.

entries.clue: Wingless bugs fused to wood boiler (9)

indicatorNotes.Wingless: the wings of a word are its outer letters, clipped off

blocks.note: teak is a hardwood
bugs = NETTLES (irritates), without its outer letters

annotation.surface: Insects without wings stuck fast to a wooden stove.
annotation.walkthrough: Wingless bugs looks like insects, but bugs is the verb to annoy, and wings are the word's end letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A teakettle is a kettle for boiling water, a boiler.

entries.clue: Meaning of speech is beyond me at first (5)

indicatorNotes.is beyond: beyond means further along, so the word for 'of speech' sits past the M
indicatorNotes.at first: only the first letter of me is used

blocks.note: first letter of Me
oral = spoken

annotation.surface: Someone admitting the point of a speech is lost on them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beyond me' reads as 'too hard for me'; here it just means placed after M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the lesson a fable teaches is its point, what it means.

entries.clue: Stars with capital backing promo (9)

indicatorNotes.backing: promo is written backing, back to front

blocks.note: and = with
Rome, capital of Italy
an ad is a promotion; backing it gives DA

annotation.surface: Celebrities whose promotional campaign has financial backing.
annotation.walkthrough: Stars, capital, backing and promo suggest showbiz finance; capital is a city and backing is the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the northern constellation named after the chained princess of Greek myth is a pattern of stars.

entries.clue: Groggy from knocking back the out-of-date capsule (5)

indicatorNotes.knocking back: to knock back is to down in one; in a down entry the letters are sent back up

blocks.note: ye is an archaic, out-of-date spelling of the
a pod is a capsule, as a seed pod or escape pod

annotation.surface: Feeling woozy after swallowing an expired pill.
annotation.walkthrough: The medicine scene makes 'knocking back' mean swallowing a pill; the phrase is the reversal signal. 'The out-of-date' is a sly way to ask for an archaic form of 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: Dopey means groggy, half-stupefied.

entries.clue: Cattle regard potential fodder (5)

blocks.note: an ox is one of the cattle
to eye is to regard

annotation.surface: Cows eyeing something they might eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The oxeye daisy grows in pasture, so it really could be the cattle's fodder; the surface nearly is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a meadow plant that grazing animals may eat.

entries.clue: Ineffective first daughter’s left holding pound tip (5)

indicatorNotes.first daughter’s left: the first D, for daughter, has left
indicatorNotes.holding: the remnant holds the pen inside

blocks.note: ineffective = DUD, minus its first D
a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

annotation.surface: A useless eldest daughter has gone, keeping hold of a pound as a tip.
annotation.walkthrough: Pound and tip suggest money; pound is an animal enclosure and tip is the verb to tilt over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: turning a thing on its end or upside down tips it.

entries.clue: Dog’s lead wound and hung out (5)

indicatorNotes.lead: the lead of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Dog
a welt is a raised mark from a blow

annotation.surface: A dog's leash was wound up and hung out to dry.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has a dog's leash wound round and hung up, but lead is its first letter and hung out means lived.
annotation.definitionFit: To hang out somewhere is informally to live there, so hung out = dwelt.

entries.clue: Top banana drink with more bananas (7)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas means crazy, so the letters go mad

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
anagram fodder, 4 letters

annotation.surface: The best banana smoothie, made with extra bananas.
annotation.walkthrough: Banana appears twice with two jobs: top banana is the boss, and bananas is the signal to scramble MORE.
annotation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, the top banana.

entries.clue: Music magazine on poor quality paper (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, on means placed after

blocks.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
Time, the news magazine

annotation.surface: A music magazine printed on cheap paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music magazine' reads as one title, but Music is the definition and magazine is Time.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated American piano music of the early 1900s.

entries.clue: Le Pen introduces distinctive manner (5)

indicatorNotes.introduces: the pen comes first, introducing LE

blocks.note: a sty is a pig pen
taken as written

annotation.surface: Marine Le Pen presenting her signature approach.
annotation.walkthrough: Le Pen is the French politician in the surface; split the name and pen is a pigsty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a writer's or dresser's recognisable way of doing things.

entries.clue: Unqualified new craftsperson carries on first part of DIY (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, on means placed after

blocks.note: DIY = do it yourself, whose first part is DO
a wright is a maker, as in playwright or wheelwright
N = new

annotation.surface: An untrained new tradesperson plugging on with a home improvement job.
annotation.walkthrough: Unqualified suggests lacking credentials, which suits the DIY scene; it means utter or absolute. The first part of DIY is a word, DO, not a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Downright and unqualified both mean absolute, as in a downright lie.
